explicit_note: The LearnedProbe-Rank architecture and hyperparameters were frozen before evaluating the new generalization datasets. No changes are permitted based on new-dataset validation results.
why_this_method_and_not_gaprank: A loss-gap-weighted pairwise ranking loss (GapRank) was tested as a candidate improvement (experiments/behavioral_competence/reports/learned_probe_gaprank_report.md). GapRank improved ETTm1 but produced statistically significant regressions on ETTh2, Weather, and Electricity, and its benefit was isolated to the one dataset that motivated it. Verdict: NO IMPROVEMENT -- KEEP ORIGINAL. The standing, frozen method is therefore the ORIGINAL LearnedProbe-Rank, trained with the plain (non-gap-weighted) pairwise ranking loss.
final_inference_rule: current window + original expert forecasts + expert disagreement -> learned diagnostic probe
probe each frozen expert (differentiable forward pass, expert weights never updated)
probe-response features (6 stats: change, early_change, late_change, slope_change, variance_change, cosine_change)
rank experts by predicted competence (ascending predicted excess loss)
fixed rank weights: raw=[K,K-1,...,1]/sum -> for K=3, rank1=0.5000, rank2=0.3333, rank3=0.1667 (see rank_decision_rule_correction below)
combine ORIGINAL (unperturbed) expert forecasts with those weights

expert_selection_protocol.rule: pooled out-of-fold MAE over 4 chronological router_train folds (train_folds), minimized over all C(5,3)=10 subsets of the expert pool, ties broken by pooled MSE then worst-fold MAE then subset name

expert_training_protocol.family: walk-forward (scripts/train_costarts_walkforward_experts.py + scripts/build_costarts_walkforward_cache.py), used for ETTh1/ETTm1/Weather/Electricity in development; ETTh2 used a separate one-off fixed-OOS-split family
expert_training_protocol.chronology: block_a=0-20%, block_b=20-40%, block_c=40-60%, validation(router_val)=60-80%, test=80-100% (fractions of each dataset's own total timestamp count)
expert_training_protocol.router_train: block_b predicted by block_a-trained (0-20%) experts, concatenated with block_c predicted by block_ab-trained (0-40%) experts -- both strictly out-of-sample for the predicting checkpoint
expert_training_protocol.router_val: 60-80% predicted by final_60 experts trained on 0-60%
expert_training_protocol.optimizer: AdamW, grad-norm clip 1.0, MSE training loss, best checkpoint selected by internal validation MAE

probe_generator.architecture: Linear(num_features->32) window projection -> Conv1d(32,32,kernel=5,pad=2) temporal mixing -> Linear(4->32) forecast-summary projection (broadcast + concat) -> head = Linear(64->32) + ReLU + Linear(32->num_features)

constraints.no_modification_outside_window: structural -- delta has exactly the shape of the input history and is only ever added to it

probe_generator.probe_input: normalized current window + 4-stat summary of the expert's OWN forecast (variance, slope, first-vs-last-observed, magnitude) -- no target, error, or expert identity

competence_scorer.architecture: Linear(input_dim->64) -> ReLU -> Linear(64->32) -> ReLU -> Linear(32->1), shared across experts, no expert-identity input
competence_scorer.normalization: per-dataset z-score of the 15 static (A+B+C) features, mean/std fit on the chronological first 80% of router_train only (feat_mean/feat_std), applied unchanged to router_val; probe-response (D) features are not separately normalized

training_objective.formula: Huber(predicted_excess_loss, actual_excess_loss, delta=1.0) + 0.25 * pairwise_ranking_loss(margin=0.05) + 0.01 * (perturbation_L2 + perturbation_mean_shift) + 0.01 * temporal_smoothness_penalty
training_objective.ranking_loss: PLAIN (non-gap-weighted) pairwise hinge ranking loss over all unordered expert pairs within a window -- experiments/behavioral_competence/probe_generator.py::pairwise_ranking_loss. loss_gap_weighted_pairwise_ranking_loss (GapRank) is explicitly NOT used.
training_objective.internal_split: chronological 80/20 split of router_train (by window index, not shuffled) used only for early stopping and temperature-grid selection
training_objective.early_stopping: best epoch = lowest internal-validation joint loss; training halts after `patience` consecutive non-improving epochs
training_objective.temperature_note: selected on the internal-validation slice only, for diagnostic/Softmax-rule comparisons; the frozen final inference rule uses fixed RANK weights and does not depend on this temperature value at all

rank_decision_rule.rule: sort experts by ascending predicted_excess_loss; raw_weights = [K, K-1, ..., 1] / sum

rank_decision_rule_correction: Every prior report/manifest in this experiment family (including an earlier draft of this file) mislabeled these weights as [0.60, 0.30, 0.10]. That figure was never actually computed by any code path -- it originated from an incorrect annotation written alongside the correct formula in run_learned_probe_mechanism_ablation.py's (never-triggered) write_frozen_manifest() function, and was echoed forward through every subsequent report. The ACTUAL, always-used rule_fixed_rank function computes [K,K-1,...,1]/sum, which is [0.5000, 0.3333, 0.1667] for K=3. Every previously reported MAE/MSE number for every 'Rank' method (C-Rank, FixedD-Rank, LearnedProbe-Rank, LearnedProbe-GapRank, LearnedProbe-FrozenProbe-GapRank, across all five development datasets) used this correct [0.5,0.333,0.167] rule consistently -- only the prose label was wrong, not any computation. This is the rule frozen here, confirmed with the user, to preserve exact numerical continuity with every already-reported development-dataset result.

preprocessing_and_normalization.expert_input_normalization: per-dataset z-score using the training-range mean/std stored in each checkpoint (channel-wise)
preprocessing_and_normalization.final_forecast_scale: ORIGINAL (raw) scale; the ensemble combination uses each expert's ORIGINAL unperturbed forecast, never a perturbed one
preprocessing_and_normalization.probe_features_scale: probe-response features are computed in std-normalized units (divided by the reference channel std) before being concatenated with the z-scored A/B/C features

generalization_extension_note: For new (generalization) datasets, this exact protocol is reused unmodified: same expert pool, same walk-forward training/caching pipeline (input_len=96, horizon=12, hidden_size=64, identical optimizer/epochs/stopping), same train-only core-selection rule, same frozen ProbeGenerator/CompetenceScorer architecture, same training objective and hyperparameters, same fixed rank rule (rule_fixed_rank, [0.5,0.333,0.167] for K=3 -- see rank_decision_rule_correction). The only additions are pure registry/plumbing entries (new dataset name -> its own checkpoint root and Bundle loader) so the existing, unmodified functions can run on new data; no methodological parameter is changed. See experiments/behavioral_competence/generalization/dataset_selection.json for the new checkpoint hashes and selected cores.
